**Paris Get‑away: 7‑Day Itinerary (Mid‑Season – May/June or September/October)** *(Assumes you’ll arrive on Day 1 and depart on Day 7. Adjust dates for your own schedule.)* | Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | |-----|---------|-----------|---------| | **1** | • Arrive at Charles de Gaulle (or Orly).
• Take the RER B to Gare du Nord, then Metro Line 4 to **Châtelet–Les Halles**.
• Check into a boutique hotel in the Marais (e.g., Hôtel Henriette) or a centrally located Airbnb. | • Lunch at **Café Charlot** (classic French bistro).
• Walk to **Place des Vosges** and stroll through the gardens. | • Dinner at **Le Coupe Chou** (cozy, romantic).
• Night walk along the Seine; see the **Pont Alexandre III** lit up. | | **2** | • Breakfast at **Du Pain et des Idées** (croissants & pain au chocolat).
• Visit the **Louvre Museum** (arrive early to avoid crowds). | • Lunch in the **Tuileries Garden** (open‑air cafés).
• Explore **Musée d’Orsay** (Impressionist masterpieces). | • Dinner at **Septime** (modern French, Michelin‑starred).
• Optional: catch a show at the **Opéra Garnier** (book tickets in advance). | | **3** | • Breakfast at **Café de Flore** (iconic left‑wing café).
• Walk to **Saint‑Germain‑en‑Laye** for a quick coffee break. | • Visit **Notre‑Dame** (exterior only, interior still under restoration).
• Walk across the **Pont Neuf** to the **Île de la Cité**. | • Dinner at **Le Petit Cler** (traditional French fare).
• Evening cruise on the Seine (Bateaux Mouches) – book a sunset ticket. | | **4** | • Breakfast at **Ladurée** (famous macarons).
• Take the Metro to **Montmartre**. | • Climb to the **Sacré‑Coeur** basilica; enjoy panoramic city views.
• Explore the **Place du Tertre** (artists’ square). | • Dinner at **La Maison Rose** (picturesque Montmartre bistro).
• Optional: live jazz at **Le Caveau de la Huchette**. | | **5** | • Breakfast at **Café Kitsuné** (hipster vibe).
• Day trip to **Versailles** (Palace, Gardens, Trianon). | • Lunch at **La Petite Venise** (inside the palace gardens).
• Return to Paris in the late afternoon. | • Dinner at **Frenchie** (modern French, reservations essential).
• Night stroll through the **Latin Quarter**. | | **6** | • Breakfast at **Le Pain Quotidien** (organic bakery).
• Visit the **Centre Pompidou** (modern art). | • Lunch at **Le Georges** (restaurant atop Pompidou).
• Explore the **Marais** again – visit **Picasso Museum** or **Musée Carnavalet**. | • Dinner at **L’Arpège** (Michelin‑starred, vegetable‑centric).
• Optional: attend a cabaret at **Moulin Rouge** (book in advance). | | **7** | • Breakfast at **Café Marly** (views of Louvre).
• Last‑minute shopping on **Rue Saint‑Honoré** (designer boutiques). | • Pack and check out of your accommodation.
• Grab a quick lunch at **L’As du Fallafel** (best falafel in the city). | • Depart from Charles de Gaulle/Orly. | --- ### Practical Tips | Topic | Recommendation | |-------|----------------| | **Transportation** | • Buy a **Paris Visite** pass (valid for 2–5 days, unlimited Metro/RER).
• For day trips (Versailles), use the RER C or a guided tour. | | **Accommodation** | • Stay within 2–3 km of a Metro station for easy access.
• Consider boutique hotels in Le Marais, Saint‑Germain, or near the Louvre. | | **Dining** | • Book reservations 2–3 weeks ahead for Michelin‑starred restaurants.
• Try local specialties: croissants, escargot, coq au vin, crème brûlée. | | **Tickets** | • Pre‑purchase tickets for Louvre, Musée d’Orsay, Sacré‑Coeur, Versailles, and any shows.
• Use the official museum apps for skip‑the‑line options. | | **Weather** | • Pack layers; Paris can be breezy in spring/fall.
• Comfortable walking shoes are a must. | | **Language** | • Basic French phrases help: “Bonjour”, “Merci”, “Où est…?”.
• Most places accept credit cards; keep some euros handy. | | **Safety** | • Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded areas.
• Avoid tourist scams by using official ticket counters. | --- ### Optional Add‑Ons | Activity | Why It’s Worthwhile | |----------|---------------------| | **Wine Tasting** | Join a guided tasting in the **Latin Quarter** or a vineyard in **Champagne** (day trip). | | **Cooking Class** | Learn to make croissants or coq au vin with a local chef. | | **Nightlife** | Explore bars in **Pigalle** or rooftop lounges like **Le Perchoir**. | | **Shopping** | Visit **Galeries Lafayette** for luxury goods and the iconic glass dome. | Enjoy your Paris adventure! If you’d like a more detailed budget breakdown, specific restaurant reservations, or a customized day‑by‑day map, just let me know.
